text:
incident-bot: ALERT: anomalous auth traffic from eu-west-1 — spike of 5xx/401 + token-reuse pattern detected for /v1/generate (sampled requests include partial bearer fragments). Pager -> maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): I’m on it. confirming paged. anyone on infra?

jonathan (infra): here. seeing a spike from a handful of IPs hitting edge-proxy, also some staging log uploads to a non-standard bucket. pulling sample.

jonathan (infra): sample log lines:
```
2026-02-14T03:12:11Z edge-proxy eu-west-1 /v1/generate 401 "Authorization: Bearer sk-***abc123" src=54.36.12.9
2026-02-14T03:12:12Z edge-proxy eu-west-1 /v1/generate 401 "Authorization: Bearer sk-***abc123" src=54.36.12.9
```

maya (oncall): that looks like token fragments repeated. could be leaked debug logs or a misconfigured forwarder. jonathan, can you confirm which bucket the staging uploader touched?

jonathan (infra): bucket: redwood-staging-logs-eu-west-1/temporary-upload/2026-02-14/. I’m seeing small archived batches with names like debug-collector-20260214.tar.gz. listing now.

sarah (devsec): tagging this as potential credentials exposure. start Killchain mitigations: 1) rotate exposed service tokens 2) block suspicious source IPs 3) lock down staging bucket ACLs 4) preserve evidence (don't delete objects).

maya (oncall): executing rotation plan for any tokens that could be in those logs. devops-bot, start runbook auth-rotate-3 and post status.

devops-bot: Runbook auth-rotate-3 started by maya (oncall). Steps: rotate SVC_EDGE_READ, invalidate prefix cache, push updated creds to edge pools. Estimated ETA 8m.

jonathan (infra): I’m adding an inline WAF rule to 54.36.12.9/32 and 13.92.45.0/24 for immediate rate block. will also restrict access to the staging bucket to a temporary deny-all except admin principal.

maya (oncall): ops-scribe, note customer impact: short-lived 401s expected for any clients using rotated tokens. we'll put a graceback route for dedicated customers if needed.

ops-scribe: noted. drafting timeline for CS and support: rotate start 03:25Z, expected mitigation 03:33Z, full rollout 03:45Z.

legal (privacy): please preserve all objects and metadata. we need access logs and object versions for forensic review. do not delete or alter naming. I'll open a brief for Privacy with the incident ID.

sarah (devsec): collecting a safe sample of leaked lines to check for PII — so far only token fragments and user-agent strings. no obvious payloads with user data in the sample. will follow up.

jonathan (infra): rotation in progress: rotated SVC_EDGE_READ and SVC_DEBUG_COLLECTOR. invalidated token cache on edge pools. updating config.

devops-bot: Rotation step complete for SVC_EDGE_READ, SVC_DEBUG_COLLECTOR. Edge pools reloaded.

maya (oncall): confirming WAF blocks in place. edge error rate back to baseline on generation endpoint. auth 401s are dropping.

ops-scribe: monitoring for any customer 401 complaints. CS queue currently shows 2 inbound tickets referencing transient 'auth failed' around 03:26Z; both are dev/test accounts. no production customers flagged yet.

sarah (devsec): pulled the archived debug tar.gz — contains debug logs with bearer fragments but no full keys. logs include origin service id=collector-42 which had a config that accidentally logged full auth headers for brief window. we’ve disabled header dumping in that service.

legal (privacy): thanks. we should prepare a short customer note if further evidence shows any production tokens were exposure. for now preserve chain and classify as "probable partial token leak".

maya (oncall): action items: jonathan - keep WAF blocks for 24h and escalate if IPs change; sarah - complete PII sweep & confirm no full keys; legal - prepare hold notice; ops-scribe - draft CS blurb 'we rotated creds and have no evidence of customer key compromise at this time'. I’ll follow up in 1h.

jonathan (infra): blocks applied and will auto-remove after 24h unless we extend.

devops-bot: Post-rotate healthcheck: /v1/generate latency normal, error rate within baseline, token cache hit ratio nominal.

maya (oncall): leaving a follow-up watch. marking this thread as incident:auth-partial-leak-1856789012. Will re-open if new data. Closing live mit coordination for now. :white_check_mark:

ops-scribe: incident summary saved to incident tracker ID 2026-02-14-1856789012.

incident-bot: NOTE: Evidence preserved at s3://forensics-hold/1856789012/ — legal and devsec notified.

maya (oncall): thanks team. great fast work.
